perishability: SOTA ground truth decays. Re-validate each item's `validated` date before treating a miss as a pipeline failure when replaying >6 months after `frozen`.

items.name: icraft2170/youtube-data-mcp-server
items.expected_mechanism: named MCP-registry sweep (official MCP Registry, Smithery, mcp.so, Glama, LobeHub, mcpservers.org)
items.accept_when: the manifest's mcp-registries findings (or the draft benchmark table) name an OAuth2-capable YouTube MCP server exposing private-playlist enumeration (getMyPlaylists or equivalent)
items.miss_root_cause: no registry sweep was planned; the declared-non-exhaustive MCP inventory (3 servers) became 'nothing exists' downstream despite a judge-refused universal

items.name: Unipile (unified messaging API)
items.expected_mechanism: stack-inventory grep BEFORE any web call (deterministic; CI uses stack-corpus/ + stack-paths.fixture.json)
items.accept_when: the own-stack sweep surfaces the unified-messaging bridge documented in the configured stack corpus as covering Instagram DMs (hosted-auth session delegation, chats/messages API, webhooks)
items.miss_root_cause: internal-stack inventory was not ritual; queries named the problem ('Instagram scraper'), not the capability class ('unified messaging API')

items.name: HikerAPI (managed public-data Instagram API, ~$0.60/1k requests)
items.expected_mechanism: vendor enumeration by risk class — managed public scraping
items.accept_when: the commercial-vendors sweep (or benchmark table) names HikerAPI or an equivalent managed public-data vendor with per-1k pricing materially below the Apify-class option
items.miss_root_cause: vendor enumeration stopped at the first priced option; no per-class cost comparison was mandated

items.name: session-delegation vendor class (e.g. Phantombuster: 'your Instagram session cookie' as input)
items.expected_mechanism: risk-class taxonomy enumeration (deterministic: the class must exist in the sweep plan and carry >=1 representative)
items.accept_when: the commercial-vendors category enumerates a session-delegation class with at least one named representative, graded by account risk — even under a credentialed NO-GO gate (a gate is a reason to enumerate better, never to stop enumerating)
items.miss_root_cause: a credentialed NO-GO gate stopped enumeration of the gated class; sub-classes with very different risk profiles were never separated

items.name: Panniantong/Agent-Reach (agent internet-capability layer)
items.expected_mechanism: GitHub-native topic-facet sweep sorted by stars (gh search repos --topic / api.github.com/search?q=topic:...&sort=stars), NOT prose search
items.accept_when: the open-source sweep surfaces a capability layer that routes per platform through an ordered preferred-then-fallback backend list with real probing — reached via a topic query, and the manifest's open-source queries carry at least one GitHub-native query
items.miss_root_cause: open-source declared 'swept' on prose queries alone; no GitHub-native query ever ran. Amplified by language (Chinese-first README, invisible to EN/FR prose) and by category vocabulary ('capability layer', 'internet reach' were not the searcher's words)

items.name: jackwener/OpenCLI (logged-in-browser control surface)
items.expected_mechanism: GitHub-native topic-facet sweep sorted by stars (topic:browser-use and neighbours)
items.accept_when: the open-source sweep surfaces a tool that drives the user's already-logged-in Chrome (navigate, click, type, extract) and ships an agent-side skill — the leading implementation of the session-reuse class
items.miss_root_cause: the run named the session-reuse class as strongest for authenticated portals, then populated it from market-comparison blogs — a class absent from those blogs by construction, since its vendors do not blog
